newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN DLR FINDS ENOUGH SUPPORT TO HOLD GAINS.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN DLR FINDS ENOUGH SUPPORT TO HOLD GAINS.

text.p: The Australian dollar found itself well supported in a snug range at the beginning of the week as it held on to the half cent gain made in offshore trade on Friday.

While the dollar remained vulnerable to a retest of the two year lows of US$0.7295 set on Friday, sentiment was helped by Friday's improvement in the gold price and some reported switching out of the Canadian dollar.
By noon (0200 GMT) the dollar was at US$0.7360/70, a slight improvement on an early US$0.7352/57 but well up on Friday's late US$0.7311/16.

With little data this week -- the major two events are a speech by RBA governor Ian Macfarlane on Tuesday and final second quarter wages data on Thursday -- attention was centred on the U.S. dollar after its heavy losses on Friday.
Those losses had fed through to the Australian dollar, which dropped more than two yen and almost one pfenning when the U.S. dollar weakened, but reclaimed some of those losses in morning trade.
By noon, the dollar was trading at 84.92/85.02 yen and 1.3617/38 marks, up on any early 84.32/42 and 1.3568/81, but still down on Friday's late 86.51/61 and 1.3633/46.
In trade weighted terms the unit had recovered from an opening dip to be level with its close to last week of 57.6.
While the U.S. dollar was dominating Asian trade, local traders said the market was waiting on Macfarlane's speech and the wages data to help clarify the interest rate outlook.
Macfarlane will be talking on monetary policy and growth, and in his first Australian speech since before the May 23 rate cut his words will be analysed for clues as to policy direction.
